'''Ambrose Jearld Jr.''' is a marine biologist who started his career as one of the first black fisheries biologists at the [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] (NOAA). He spent his nearly 40-year career at the Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC) in [[Woods Hole, Massachusetts]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Envisioning diversity in science with Dr. Ambrose Jearld {{!}} National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration|url=https://www.noaa.gov/heritage/stories/envisioning-diversity-in-science-with-dr-ambrose-jearld|access-date=2020-08-06|website=noaa.gov|date=22 July 2020 }}</ref> The lecture series named after him in Woods Hole reflects his career-long commitment to increasing diversity in environmental and fisheries sciences.

== Early life and education ==
Ambrose Jearld Jr. grew up on a family farm in [[Orrum, North Carolina]] and became interested in science during high school. <ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Ambrose Jearld, Nat'l Marine Fisheries S'vc {{!}} sitesALIVE!|url=https://vg2016.sitesalive.com/en/experts/dr-ambrose-jearld/|access-date=2020-08-06|website=vg2016.sitesalive.com}}</ref>
[[File:Honey gourami red variant.jpg|alt=small golden in a tank with plants|thumb|Honey Gourami studied by Ambrose Jearld Jr. for his dissertation at [[Oklahoma State University–Stillwater]]]]
In 1965, Jearld earned a BS from what is now called the [[University of Maryland Eastern Shore]], with a major in [[Biology]] and a minor in [[Chemistry]].<ref name=":1" />  After graduating, he worked for a few years as a chemist at Publicker Industries Inc. in Philadelphia.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=Fisheries|first=NOAA|date=2021-08-11|title=Ambrose Jearld, Jr.: Researcher, Educator, Mentor and Advocate for Diversity and Inclusion {{!}} NOAA Fisheries|url=https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/ambrose-jearld-jr-researcher-educator-mentor-and-advocate-diversity-and-inclusion|access-date=2021-08-13|website=NOAA|language=en}}</ref> In 1967, he was recruited by Bradford Brown to begin a fully-funded Masters program at [[Oklahoma State University–Stillwater]].<ref name=":6" /> In 1969, he was [[Draft lottery (1969)|drafted into the army]] during the Vietnam war and was posted in Maryland at a Medical Research Laboratory where he was able to conduct biological research. During this time in the military, Jearld also worked on his MS research on [[Channel catfish]], earning his degree in 1970 from Oklahoma State University–Stillwater. After completing his military service in 1971, Jearld had several offers to attend doctoral programs but chose to return to Oklahoma State University–Stillwater for a PhD, working with his advisor, Rudy Miller.<ref name=":6" /> His zoology dissertation research on the sexual behavior of the [[Honey gourami]] earned him his PhD in 1975.<ref name=":4">{{Cite book|last1=Kessler|first1=James H.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-ydHVdMUqdEC&pg=PA189|title=Distinguished African American Scientists of the 20th Century|last2=Morin|first2=Katherine A.|last3=Kidd|first3=J. S.|last4=Kidd|first4=Renee A.|date=1996|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-89774-955-8|language=en}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After earning his PhD Jearld worked as an assistant professor of biology at [[Lincoln University (Pennsylvania)]] from 1975 until 1977 when he took an assistant professor position at [[Howard University]].<ref name=":4" /> During this time, he took advantage of short-term research opportunities at different locations across the country, including studies of anchovy in San Francisco Bay in collaboration with [[Lawrence Livermore Laboratory]] and the University of California.<ref name=":6" />

Jearld spent the summer of 1977 doing research with marine animals at the center's [[Sandy Hook Laboratory]] in New Jersey, and the summer of 1978 on a part-time appointment at the Woods Hole Laboratory. That summer, a permanent federal research position in [[Falmouth, Massachusetts]] was announced, which Jearld applied for, and was hired.<ref name=":6" /> Jearld worked at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC) from 1978 until his retirement in 2016.

At the time of his hiring, Jearld was the first black researcher with a doctorate degree at NEFSC.<ref name=":0" /> He joined a group that was tasked with acquiring biological information to assess the populations and stocks of important fishery resources.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Black History Month Blog Series 2020: Ambrose Jearld Jr. – Broader Impacts Group|url=https://web.whoi.edu/big/black-history-month-blog-series-2020-ambrose-jearld-jr/|access-date=2020-08-06|language=en-US}}</ref>  The group collected data on a wide range of metrics including age, which has resulted a robust and well-known data set of age composition for many fish and shellfish species.<ref name=":2" />  Jearld contributed to several studies on techniques for age determination including [[optical Fourier transform]] analysis of fish scales and definition of growth lines from microstructure of ocean [[quahog]] shells.<ref name=":2" /> He also authored the chapter on Age Determination in ''Fishery Techniques'', an oft cited reference for fisheries scientists.

In 1985, Jearld became chief of the Research Planning and Evaluation Section, and in 1997 became chief of the Research Planning and Coordination. in 2004, he became the Director of Academic Programs, the position he eventually retired from in 2016.<ref name=":5" />

In his role as a biologist and administrator, Jearld has advised the [[NOAA]] on national and international affairs in South Africa. He was appointed to the US - South African Bi-Lateral Commission's Working Group on Fisheries and he worked with Sea Fisheries, South Africa, on development and implementation of a series of reforms including restructuring and outreach. He has been involved in NOAA science and technical support for six West African countries around the [[Gulf of Guinea]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=August 6, 2020|title=Dr. Ambrose Jearld, Jr.|url=https://www.umes.edu/uploadedFiles/_WEBSITES/MHEBRC/Content/PresenterParticipantBios/Bio_Ambrose%20Jearld.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

=== Diversity initiatives ===
Jearld was the first chair of the Woods Hole Diversity Advisory Committee, a six-institution collaboration started in 2004 to promote diversity and inclusion across the [[NOAA]] Northeast Fisheries Science Center, [[Marine Biological Laboratory]], [[Sea Education Association]], [[United States Geological Survey]], [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]], and [[Woods Hole Research Center]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Woods Hole Scientific Community Diversity Initiative|url=https://www.woodsholediversity.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/19/2019/09/whdiversity_mou_withsignatures.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120211543/https://www.woodsholediversity.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/19/2019/09/whdiversity_mou_withsignatures.pdf |archive-date=2022-01-20 |access-date=6 August 2020|website=woods hole diversity}}</ref> Ambrose Jearld Jr. was the co-founder of the [https://www.woodsholediversity.org/pep/ Partnership Education Program (PEP)] and served as its Director from its inception in 2009 until 2016, when he retired.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PEP - Woods Hole Diversity|url=https://www.woodsholediversity.org/pep/|access-date=2020-08-06|website=woodsholediversity.org|language=en-US}}</ref> PEP recruits mainly junior and senior undergraduate students from underrepresented groups interested in marine and environmental sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Fisheries|first=NOAA|date=2018-05-11|title=Partnership in Education Program Begins 10th Year {{!}} NOAA Fisheries|url=https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/partnership-education-program-begins-10th-year|access-date=2020-08-06|website=NOAA|language=en}}</ref> In 2017, the Woods Hole scientific community launched an [https://www.woodsholediversity.org/events/ambrose-jearld-jr-lecture/ annual lectureship] named in his honor.

== Honors and recognition ==
* 2021 [https://eos.org/agu-news/congratulations-to-the-2021-agu-union-medal-award-and-prize-recipients American Geophysical Union] Ambassador Awardee
*Inaugural class of [[American Fisheries Society]] Fellows in 2015<ref>{{Cite web|title=AFS Fellows Program {{!}} American Fisheries Society|url=https://fisheries.org/about/awards-recognition/call-for-award-nominations/afs-fellows-program/|access-date=2020-08-06|website=fisheries.org}}</ref>
* Leadership Council of the [[American Geophysical Union]]<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Lectureship honors Ambrose Jearld, Jr. for promoting diversity|url=https://www.sea.edu/sea_currents/single/lectureship_honors_ambrose_jearld_jr._for_promoting_div|access-date=2020-08-06|website=SEA Semester {{!}} Sea Education Association|language=en}}</ref>
* 2004 Member of the [[Sea Education Association]] Board of Trustees<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Study Abroad with SEA Semester {{!}} Sea Education Association {{!}} SEA Semester|url=https://www.sea.edu/about_sea/trustees_and_overseers|access-date=2020-08-06|website=sea.edu}}</ref>
* 2007 Member of the [[Massachusetts Maritime Academy]] Board of Trustees<ref name=":3" />
* 2017 The [http://woodsholediversity.org/ Woods Hole Diversity Initiative]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ambrose Jearld, Jr. Lecture - Woods Hole Diversity|url=https://www.woodsholediversity.org/events/ambrose-jearld-jr-lecture/|access-date=2020-08-06|website=woodsholediversity.org|language=en-US}}</ref> launched the annual Ambrose Jearld Jr. lectureship recognizing Jearld's work on improving diversity and inclusion within the ocean sciences community.<ref name=":3" /> Speakers have included David J. Asai (2017),  [[Ashanti Johnson]] (2018), [[Warren M. Washington]] (2019) and Nigel Golden (2020).
